definition: Helsinki Finite-State Technology (HFST) is a computer programming library and set of utilities for natural language processing with finite-state automata and finite-state transducers.
details: It is free and open-source software, released under a mix of the GNU General Public License version 3 (GPLv3) and the Apache License.

explainer.lead: HFST, short for Helsinki Finite-State Technology, is a free, open-source programming library and set of utilities for processing language with finite-state machines. It helps software recognize patterns in text or transform one sequence of symbols into another.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a little machine that follows a map as it reads a word, one letter at a time. Some maps say whether the word belongs to an allowed set, while others change it into something new. HFST gives programmers tools for using these maps with language.
tiers.practitioner: HFST provides a programming library and utilities for applying finite-state automata and transducers in natural-language-processing software. Automata recognize strings, while transducers produce output strings as they process input. When redistributing software, check the applicable license terms because HFST uses a mix of GPLv3 and the Apache License.
tiers.paperLevel: A finite-state automaton defines a set of strings through transitions between a finite collection of states. A finite-state transducer additionally associates outputs with transitions, defining a relation between input and output strings. HFST supplies library and utility support for using these formalisms in natural language processing.

explainer.example: A transducer could be designed to read the token "cats" and emit "cat +PL", representing the base form and a plural marker. HFST provides the finite-state technology through which such a mapping can be used in a language-processing program.

usedIn.name: Natural language processing
usedIn.detail: Software can use finite-state automata and transducers to recognize or transform sequences of text symbols.

usedIn.name: Open-source language tooling
usedIn.detail: HFST can be incorporated through its programming library or used through its accompanying utilities.

explainer.intuition: A finite-state machine is like a small flowchart that moves between states as it reads symbols. HFST lets language software use these machines either to decide whether an input fits a pattern or to turn the input into a related output.
howItWorks: Represent the allowed states and the transitions between them.
Read the input sequence symbol by symbol and follow the applicable transitions.
Use an automaton when the goal is to recognize whether a sequence is accepted.
Use a transducer when transitions must also emit symbols, producing an output sequence.
Access the technology through HFST's programming library or its utilities.
explainer.whyItMatters: HFST makes finite-state automata and transducers available as reusable open-source software rather than requiring every project to implement the machinery itself. Its library and utilities support both integration into programs and direct tool-based use.
misconceptions: HFST is a library and collection of utilities, not a learned language model.
An automaton recognizes strings; a transducer can also transform input into output.
HFST is not released under one single license: its licensing mixes GPLv3 and the Apache License.
